name: Studio lead
role: Runs the table, keeps the record, and says what happens next.
judges: Opens each stage, reconciles the experts, and turns their findings into either a pass or one short revision.

name: Architect
role: Decides what kind of room this palette wants, and why.
judges: Proposes two or three room ideas for the palette, then proportions, openings and circulation. On the image: is this the room that was designed?

name: Builder
role: Asks whether it could actually be built.
judges: Structure, junctions, windows and details, before and after the image. Advisory; never a building-code check.

name: Interior designer
role: Places every colour and every piece of furniture.
judges: Where each palette colour goes and how much of it, the furnishings, and the hierarchy of the room.

name: Colour specialist
role: Invents the studio's palettes, reads every palette first, and measures it last.
judges: Makes new studio palettes and series by the rules in Guide §4; reads how a palette's colours relate in lightness, strength and temperature; then measures colour on each surface of the image against the palette.

name: Photographer
role: Owns the light, the lens and the viewpoint.
judges: Neutral daylight that keeps the colours true, camera height and lens, where the eye lands; then whether the image looks photographed.

name: Stylist
role: Makes it look lived in, and takes things away.
judges: Believability and restraint: signs of life, nothing staged, nothing cloned, no stray accent colours.

name: Composition editor
role: Thinks only about the finished post on a phone.
judges: The room and swatches side by side as a social post: crop, hierarchy, legibility on a phone, whether it stops a scroll.
